question: On 24 June 2026, two devastating earthquakes hit Venezuela, triggering a humanitarian disaster of great magnitude. With 119 Portuguese nationals and people of Portuguese descent already confirmed among the dead, not to mention those still missing, Europe’s response must be swift, robust and commensurate with the sheer scale of the disaster and the way in which it is unfolding on the ground.

The Commission has activated the EU Civil Protection Mechanism and deployed the Copernicus emergency mapping service, but has announced just EUR 5 million in humanitarian aid to top up the EUR 52 million in regular aid already planned prior to the disaster. In light of the above: 1.

Can the Commission say precisely what emergency support the Commission has already mobilised for Venezuela, indicating the financial, human, logistical and technical resources deployed, and whether the EUR 5 million pledged are deemed sufficient given the scale of the disaster?

What type of assistance – for example, search-and-rescue operations, medical support, temporary accommodation, telecommunications, emergency mapping services and protection of the most vulnerable – is being provided on the ground?

What additional measures is the Commission planning, in cooperation with the Member States, to step up the humanitarian response and support the communities affected, and does it undertake to provide regular updates on the actual implementation and the transparent use of the aid deployed?
Supporters1
This question is supported by Members other than the authors: Nora Junco García (ECR), Diego Solier (ECR), Alvise Pérez (NI). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.9.2026) In the immediate aftermath of the disaster, the EU Civil Protection Mechanism1 (UCPM) was activated on 25 June 2026, following the request for assistance from Venezuela. The Commission’s Emergency Response Coordination Centre (ERCC) coordinated with Member States and the Venezuelan authorities the delivery of assistance2.

Around 750 responders and tonnes of relief items have been mobilised from 19 countries. This includes search and rescue, emergency medical teams, a telecommunication module, a structural engineering team, medicines, shelters among others. Final deliveries under the UCPM are being planned, after which the operation is expected to conclude3.

The EU’s Copernicus satellite service4 provided emergency mapping to support operations on the ground. Under ReliefEU5, five Humanitarian Air Bridge flights have carried over 214 tonnes of emergency supplies, of which 57 tonnes were donated from EU stockpiles6. On 15 July 2026, the EU announced EUR 20 million in support for the earthquake response in Venezuela7.

This adds to the EUR 5 million life-saving assistance already approved at the end of June 2026, and to the EUR 52 million allocated at the beginning of the year to respond to the humanitarian consequences of the socio-economic crisis in Venezuela8. EU-funded humanitarian assistance is needs-based and channelled through humanitarian partners, in accordance with the humanitarian principles.

It is delivered within the framework of the established humanitarian coordination architecture, under the leadership of UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)9. The Commission will continue to keep the Member States and European Parliament updated.

1 https://civil-protection-humanitarian-aid.ec.europa.eu/what/civil-protection/eu-civil-protection-mechanism_en. 2 A European Civil Protection Team was deployed to strengthen coordination efforts on the ground - 10 experts,

1 ERCC Liaison Officer and 1 Rapid Response Coordinator. 3 UCPM assistance from Portugal and Greece. 4 https://mapping.emergency.copernicus.eu/activations/EMSR884/. 5 https://civil-protection-humanitarian-aid.ec.europa.eu/what/humanitarian-aid/reliefeu_en. 6 In addition, one information management officer, two logistics officers and one emergency medical team have been deployed with support from ReliefEU.

7 Comprising EUR 10 million in additional humanitarian funding to help the most affected communities and EUR 10 million, subject to approval by the Budgetary Authority, including to support the search and rescue, medical and other expert teams’ operation, as well as in-kind assistance; https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/mex_26_1621.
8 EUR 52 million represent the EU’s humanitarian response both inside and outside Venezuela. 9 The UN Humanitarian Coordinator and the internationally mandated coordination body.
